base_source: TTM through Q2 2026 from 10-Q YTD figures: OCF $1,394.102M (FY25 $1,370.133M - H1'25 $622.366M + H1'26 $646.335M) - capex $279.332M ($415.034M - $275.313M + $139.611M) - SBC ~$12.854M (not broken out in 10-Q; held at FY25 level) = $1,101.916M / 209.014M diluted shares = $5.27/share
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.2%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
moat_justification: Structural cost advantage (OR 70.1% Q2 2026 vs industry mid-80s) from network density, owned service centers and a non-union low-turnover workforce; service quality (99% on-time, 0.1% claims) converts to pricing power (4.9% GRI Oct 2026, rev/cwt +5.5% ex-fuel with volumes down); ~35% spare capacity and a net-cash balance sheet let it take share through cycles — against low switching costs/annual bids, no network effects, capable rivals (XPO, Saia, FedEx Freight, Estes) investing to close the service gap, and freight cyclicality (revenue -5.5% in 2025, tons/day still -4.1% in Q2 2026).
name: Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc.
one_liner: Strong-moat (7/10) best-in-class LTL carrier with real pricing power and a net-cash balance sheet, but at $181.30 (34x TTM owner's earnings of $5.27/share, 2.9% yield) it yields a 6.0% weighted IRR — clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$49 (~$39 with a margin of safety); even the super-bull case ($99.20) is far below today's price.
